Ivo Andrić was a novelist, born in 1892 near Travnik in central Bosnia, who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1961.

Born to a Catholic Croat family, he joined the Young Bosnia movement as a student and was jailed by Austria after the Sarajevo assassination. He became a diplomat of the Yugoslav kingdom and was its envoy in Berlin when Germany invaded in 1941. In occupied Belgrade he wrote his great Bosnian novels, The Bridge on the Drina, about the bridge at Višegrad, and Bosnian Chronicle, set in Travnik. They show Bosnia as a place where Muslims, Christians and Jews lived side by side with deep mistrust. Croats, Serbs and Bosniaks all claim him.
sum: Ivo Andrić was a novelist, born in 1892 near Travnik in central Bosnia, who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1961.
